steering_ledger.stage2_response: Answered in-session (see reply 2026-07-28): we do not care about them as production candidates; we care because (a) reasoning-compression.md maintains a standing watch on looped/latent-reasoning models as potential small-role candidates (Ouro was filed as a CPU-verifier idea, intake-332), (b) the lineage's promise — test-time compute knob converting loops into quality without parameter growth — matches our routed multi-role stack shape, and (c) a smoke test is the cheapest way to convert credibility-1 self-reported claims into first-party evidence before any investment. The honest caveat from intake-902's own justification stands: looping cuts parameter FOOTPRINT, not per-token DRAM traffic, so the CPU-decode-BW win is unproven — which is precisely what a smoke test would measure. Whether the smoke-test actionable survives into the Stage-3 plan is for the operator after dives land.

looped-transformers-overview-2026-07-28.title: Looped Transformers: Reusing Model Parameters for Scalable Reasoning Through Recurrent Depth
looped-transformers-overview-2026-07-28.provenance: unstated — reads as a synthesized technical overview; no URL, no author byline; final line says content is 'drawn from the technical overview of looped Transformer research'
summary_of_claims: Looped/recurrent-depth/latent-reasoning models reuse a shared layer block iterated in depth; ~4x parameter reduction at comparable FLOPs/latency

UT (1807.03819) is the ancestor: shared transition function + ACT halting; did not dominate due to compute-vs-parameter tradeoff at matched FLOPs, timing vs the scaling era, encoder-decoder-only evaluation, modest gains
Modern designs: prelude/core/coda partition, truncated backprop through time, randomly sampled loop count r replacing learned ACT halting; r is a continuous inference-time quality knob
Huginn (Geiping et al. 2502.05171): 3.5B/800B tokens, unrolled depth matches up to ~50B-parameter-equivalent reasoning on certain benchmarks, latent-space reasoning without CoT tokens

MoEUT (2405.16039): loops fine-grained expert groups to restore capacity; Relaxed Recursive Transformers (2410.20672): per-step LoRA adapters on shared block; MoR (2507.10524): token-level routing to recursion depth + KV-sharing variant
DeepLoop (2607.13491): loop-aware DeepNorm scaling exponent fixing training instability from weight reuse [IDENTITY UNVERIFIED]
Loopie (2607.16051): layer-wise looping (A-A-A-B-B-B) + reduced stored depth + MoE reinvestment, claimed to surpass compute-matched vanilla Transformer [IDENTITY UNVERIFIED]
